sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

No information is available on the clinical use of saxagliptin during breastfeeding. Saxagliptin has a shorter half-life than the other dipeptidyl-peptidase IV inhibitors, so it might be a better choice among drugs in this class for nursing mothers. Monitoring of the breastfed infant's blood glucose is advisable during maternal therapy with saxagliptin. However, an alternate drug may be preferred, especially while nursing a newborn or preterm infant.
